title: Reni (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: Alan John 'Reni' Wren, born 10 April 1964, Manchester; grew up in Gorton; self-taught. Joined the Stone Roses in May 1984 (ripped their advert off the wall of A1 Music); left in March 1995 (Robbie Maddix after him); the Rub 1998-2001; the reunion 2011-2017. 'His laid-back style of complex, off-beat rhythms was influential in bringing about the blend of indie and dance music which formed much of the Madchester sound.' Early on 'energy from influences such as Keith Moon'; from Sally Cinnamon (1987) a three-piece kit, 'a mixture of Ludwig, vintage, and a big expensive Sonor snare drum', painted by John Squire; 'busy use of the high-hat, snare, and solitary tom-tom'. Second Coming: 'extra tom-toms for a style analogous to John Bonham'. Matched grip, traditional on TV for One Love and Fools Gold (1990). Rhythm (2004): 'funkier and more subtle than any drummer in the genre had ever been', 'economical, soulful, and inventive'. Jon Brookes (the Charlatans): 'He never pounded the drums, he used to caress them'. John Robb: 'he could hit hard like a rock drummer but also had a real swing'. Pete Townshend borrowed him for his set in 1984 and called him 'the most natural drummer I've seen since Keith Moon'. Leckie: 'every tom, cymbal and drum is from a different kit'. The bucket hat. The reunion kit: two bass drums, more toms and cymbals.

title: The Stone Roses (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 2 May 1989 by Silvertone; recorded mostly at Battery Studios, London, with John Leckie, June 1988 to February 1989. Leckie found the demos' tempos too fast and gave them 'intros and outros, and steady tempos'. I Am the Resurrection's coda: Leckie told them to 'do something melodic'. Personnel: Reni, drums, backing vocals, piano on She Bangs the Drums.

title: Fools Gold (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Double A-side with What the World Is Waiting For, 13 November 1989; recorded at Sawmills Studios, Cornwall. 'Ian Brown stated the song was written over "The Funky Drummer" by James Brown, which Reni had to learn the beat from.' Bass line after Young MC's Know How.

title: Second Coming (The Stone Roses album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 5 December 1994 by Geffen; recorded at Forge Studios, Oswestry, and Rockfield, 1992-1994. Reni: drums, backing vocals, vocals on Tightrope.

title: I Am the Resurrection - Wikipedia
notes: Reni: the track 'originated when bassist Mani played the riff of The Beatles' "Taxman" backwards ... Mani would play the riff backwards during sound-checks and we played along over the top for a laugh.' The last four minutes are an instrumental outro.

title: Love Spreads - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 21 November 1994, number two in the UK, the first from Second Coming.

title: How James Brown and Johnny Cash inspired a classic song by The Stone Roses (Jordan Potter, Far Out)
notes: 17 January 2023. John Squire: 'That's where I heard the "Funky Drummer" loop that we built "Fools Gold" around.' 'Instead of simply sampling the source track, Reni took it upon himself to learn the beat' and added flourishes of his own. Others (The Quietus) hear Bobby Byrd's Hot Pants instead; not settled here.

title: Listen to Reni's isolated drums on The Stone Roses' 'Love Spreads' (Tyler Golsen, Far Out)
notes: 27 January 2022: She Bangs the Drums, I Am the Resurrection and Waterfall as rhythm workouts: 'anyone who has tried to replicate those patterns quickly finds out just how difficult they actually are'; Love Spreads 'propelled by ... rock steady rhythms from Reni'.
